blocks.text: Imagine you need to prove a mathematical statement from a set of assumptions. How do you systematically derive the conclusion? Welcome to the world of natural deduction!

blocks.markdown: Natural deduction is a proof system used to derive conclusions from premises using a set of inference rules. It mirrors the way humans naturally reason, hence its name. In this lesson, we will explore the introduction and elimination rules, and how assumptions are used and discharged.

blocks.title: Natural Deduction
blocks.text: A proof system that uses a set of inference rules to derive conclusions from premises, closely resembling human reasoning.

blocks.markdown: In natural deduction, each logical connective (like \(\land\), \(\lor\), \(\rightarrow\), \(\neg\)) has associated introduction and elimination rules. These rules define how to introduce or eliminate the connective in a proof.

blocks.latex: \begin{align*} \text{Conjunction Introduction (}\land\text{I)}: & \quad \frac{A, B}{A \land B} \\ \text{Conjunction Elimination (}\land\text{E)}: & \quad \frac{A \land B}{A} \quad \text{or} \quad \frac{A \land B}{B} \\ \text{Implication Introduction (}\rightarrow\text{I)}: & \quad \frac{[A] \vdots B}{A \rightarrow B} \\ \text{Implication Elimination (}\rightarrow\text{E)}: & \quad \frac{A \rightarrow B, A}{B} \end{align*}
blocks.caption: Basic rules of natural deduction for conjunction and implication.

blocks.markdown: Let's explore these rules with examples. Consider the statement: If it rains, the ground will be wet. We can represent this as \(R \rightarrow W\).

blocks.title: Proving a Simple Implication
blocks.answer: The conclusion \(W\) is derived using the assumption \(R\) and the implication \(R \rightarrow W\).

blocks.markdown: In the example above, we used the Implication Elimination rule. Now, let's look at how assumptions are discharged using Implication Introduction.

blocks.title: Discharging an Assumption
blocks.prompt: Show that \(P \rightarrow (Q \rightarrow P)\) is a tautology.

steps.text: 4. Discharge \(Q\) using Implication Introduction (\(\rightarrow\text{I}\)) to get \(Q \rightarrow P\).
5. Discharge \(P\) using Implication Introduction (\(\rightarrow\text{I}\)) to get \(P \rightarrow (Q \rightarrow P)\).

blocks.answer: The statement \(P \rightarrow (Q \rightarrow P)\) is proven by discharging assumptions \(Q\) and \(P\).

blocks.title: Assumption Discharge
blocks.text: In natural deduction, assumptions are discharged when they are no longer needed, typically through the use of Implication Introduction.

points: Natural deduction uses introduction and elimination rules for logical connectives.
Assumptions can be discharged using Implication Introduction.
